exposure: Antibiotic treatment during the first 2 years of life
cohort: 90 children followed longitudinally from birth to 7 years of age
finding: Oral microbiome composition changes over time, with early colonization by Streptococcus and Veillonella, and later colonization by other genera such as Neisseria, and these patterns are influenced by mode of delivery, breastfeeding duration, and antibiotic use.
mod_finding: Infants born by C-section had initially skewed bacterial content compared with vaginally delivered infants, but this was recovered with age.
